protections: The global list of configured GitHub Enterprise endpoints (name + API URL returned by GitHubConfiguration.getEndpoints()) may be returned by a descriptor form fill only to a caller holding Jenkins.MANAGE when the call has no item ancestor, or Item.EXTENDED_READ when the call is item-scoped, while still returning the full list to item-scoped callers who legitimately configure the item.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: doFillApiUriItems takes no arguments and performs no check, and its only caller in the UI is the organization-folder/new-item jelly which already hides the picker behind isApiUriSelectable, so a solver can assume only users who can configure an item ever cause the list to be built; descriptor form fills are in fact individually addressable by any Overall/Read caller.

This is a second, inline copy of the same loop rather than a call to GitHubSCMNavigator.getPossibleApiUriItems(), and the SCM Source picker is only rendered from a job/folder configure page (config-detail.jelly:26-30), so a solver can accept 'whoever reaches it has Item/CONFIGURE' and can also assume that fixing the navigator helper covers this copy; it does not, because the loop is duplicated here.

The method is a one-line delegate to the navigator's static helper through a static import (line 3) in the credentials descriptor, so a solver can assume a guard placed in that helper covers it, and can assume GitHub App credentials are only managed by users with Jenkins.MANAGE; folder-scoped credential stores are managed by users holding Item.CONFIGURE on the folder, who need the endpoint list and would be blanked by an unconditional Jenkins.MANAGE check.

The package already contains two neighbouring idioms a solver can copy instead of the context-dependent guard: an unconditional Jenkins.get().checkPermission(Jenkins.MANAGE) on the SECURITY-3702 method (GitHubAppCredentials.java:839-848) and @RequirePOST on check methods; reusing them blanks the endpoint picker for folder configurators who hold only Item.CONFIGURE and a POST-only rule stops the <f:select/> fill from loading at all.

It returns only a boolean (whether at least one GHE endpoint exists), never a URL, and the jelly needs it to decide whether to render the picker; the advisory is about enumerating endpoint URLs, so this is an existence oracle only, and it has no item context so it cannot express the context-dependent rule.

This trait descriptor already applies exactly the required context == null ? Jenkins.MANAGE : Item.EXTENDED_READ guard to its own credentials fill (lines 154-157), so an endpoint picker added beside it looks as if it was reviewed with the same rule, and a solver who has fixed the three reported descriptors has no reason to open a trait file at all.

The global configuration page itself requires Jenkins.MANAGE (GitHubConfiguration.java:238-242), so an endpoint form fill added to this descriptor looks protected by the page; getRequiredGlobalConfigPagePermission does not cover the descriptor-named form fill URL, which remains individually addressable.

This descriptor already exposes form-fill/validation methods for app-scoped data with no item-context guard, so a GHE-server chooser added to the repository-access strategy looks like ordinary strategy configuration in a different package that the report never mentions.

conflicts.what: The obvious fix for the boolean existence oracle (a Jenkins.MANAGE check inside isApiUriSelectable, GitHubSCMNavigator.java:1891-1893) makes the jelly hide the endpoint picker from item-scoped configurators (config.jelly:5-9), i.e. it destroys the same must-keep value T1 has to preserve; a getter with no item context cannot express the MANAGE-for-root / EXTENDED_READ-for-item rule.

One consolidated endpoint-listing helper cannot carry one unconditional rule: the root-scoped global configuration fill (T6) must require Jenkins.MANAGE, while T1 and T3 must return the list to Item.EXTENDED_READ callers; collapsing them into a single check that does not branch on the ancestor item makes one side wrong.

fairness_risks: Must-keep: an item-scoped caller holding Item.CONFIGURE (which satisfies the Item.EXTENDED_READ branch, as exercised for user bob in GitHubSCMNavigatorTest.doFillScanCredentials, src/test/java/org/jenkinsci/plugins/github_branch_source/GitHubSCMNavigatorTest.java:553-563) must still receive the full endpoint list so a folder admin can pick a GHE server (GitHubSCMNavigator/config.jelly:5-9); a rule demanding Jenkins.MANAGE on these fills contradicts legitimate folder configuration.

Must-keep: the picker is an <f:select/> form fill (GitHubAppCredentials/config.jelly:8-11) fetched without POST, so a rule that the endpoint guard must be @POST/checkPermission(Jenkins.MANAGE) (the SECURITY-3702 idiom at GitHubAppCredentials.java:839-848, which is a validate button per config.jelly:38-40) breaks the UI for every user, not just attackers.

Must-keep: isApiUriSelectable must keep answering the jelly while the configure page is rendered (GitHubAppCredentials/config.jelly:8, GitHubSCMSource/config-detail.jelly:26, GitHubSCMNavigator/config.jelly:5); it has no item context, so any required check on it is either a false denial for folder admins or a no-op.

For the credentials descriptor (T3) the ancestor Item is only present if Stapler resolves the descriptor fill under the item; if a required check assumes a non-null item there, folder-scoped credential creation by non-MANAGE users is refused, so the accepted shape must be null-safe with the MANAGE branch.

design.why: The pinned advisory-grade stack is two independent groups: G1 = T1+T3+T8, the context-dependent guard that must be applied wherever the shared getPossibleApiUriItems() output is exposed (navigator fill and credentials delegate both go through that helper, so one guard design closes them, while its must-keep side is that item-scoped Item.CONFIGURE callers keep the full list - T8), and G2 = T2, the inline duplicate loop in GitHubSCMSource that the helper fix does not reach. T4 is present in the pinned code but excluded from the graded design: requiring a permission on isApiUriSelectable cannot be expressed with an item context and would itself break the coupled value, so it is recorded as a conflict, not a trap. To reach four to five independent traps the design must use the injection room: T5 is the strongest plant (a trait descriptor one file away that already shows the exact guard for its credentials fill, so the omission looks deliberate) and T6 is the second (a global-configuration descriptor whose page-level MANAGE requirement invites forgetting that descriptor fills are individually addressable), giving four independent traps with three distinct dismissal arguments (jelly gating / duplicate-of-the-helper / global-page-requires-MANAGE) and both a deepseek-type (T2, T5, T6: protection absent plus a reason to accept it) and a mimo-type (T8: the item-scoped list a naive @POST + Jenkins.MANAGE copy destroys). This beats a design built on T4 (untestable without contradicting the UI) and beats a design that only grades T1/T3 (one judgement applied twice, no duplicate-implementation or injected-sibling pressure, and a solver who guards only the reported method never has to reconcile the helper with its two callers). Swapping T5 for T7 (different package, app-credentials strategy) is the alternative if two same-package plants are judged too similar; without planting, the real stack is only two groups.

unverified: The exact text of GHSA-G7C6-WXJF-8564 / CVE-2026-57285 was not available offline; tiers assume the report names the plugin and the endpoint-list exposure without naming the three descriptor methods (a report that names them would lower T1/T2/T3 to easy).

The published fix commit d869797365462234fe061c74fe6bf0bcae8777ea and the screener's fix.diff are not in this worktree, so whether the guard ended up in the shared getPossibleApiUriItems() or was copied into each method is inferred from the screener's fix_sites and the static import at GitHubAppCredentials.java:3; the grouping of T1 and T3 assumes a shared/context-aware guard.

Whether Stapler injects @AncestorInPath Item for a credentials descriptor's form fill (GitHubAppCredentials.DescriptorImpl) is not exercised anywhere in this repository - only SCM source/navigator/trait descriptors do (GitHubSCMSource.java:2084, GitHubSCMNavigator.java:1852, SSHCheckoutTrait.java:151) - so the item branch for T3 is unverified.
Whether isApiUriSelectable is reachable as a descriptor property URL (/descriptorByName/<class>/apiUriSelectable) was not verified; only the jelly usage is evidenced.

GitHubConfiguration.getEndpoints() is a public getter on a GlobalConfiguration/Descriptor (GitHubConfiguration.java:69-71); whether Stapler exposes it (or the endpoint objects under it) to Overall/Read callers was not verified and it is therefore not counted as a trap.

ApiRateLimitChecker.java:231-242 writes the first configured endpoint's API URL into a LogTaskListener at INFO; not counted as a trap because no attacker-controlled input reaches it and its audience is the server log - who can read that log was not verified.

Interpretation of history.a_fix_leaves_b_open: the SECURITY-3702 fix at this pinned commit (205fd59) guards doTestConnection in the same descriptor class (GitHubAppCredentials.java:839-848, test GitHubAppCredentialsDescriptorTest.java:40-74) but did not guard doFillApiUriItems in that class (818-822) or the two sibling descriptors; it is an incomplete sibling fix, not a regression, and it is a different advisory from this candidate's.
